title: CurvAdapt
subtitle: A Grasshopper plug-in for segmentation and simplification of NURBS and polylines in Building Performance Simulation
description: CurvAdapt provides a transparent and controllable framework for preparing simulation-ready geometry. It bridges the gap between free-form NURBS design models and the strict planar requirements of engines like EnergyPlus and Radiance. The plug-in integrates segmentation and simplification workflows with robust error control, ensuring geometric fidelity and improving both computational efficiency and reproducibility.

content_blocks.title: Overview
content_blocks.subtitle: Why Geometry Preparation Matters
content_blocks.content: Accurate geometry preprocessing is essential for reliable energy and daylight simulations. Modern NURBS-based design environments produce smooth, free-form curves, but simulation engines like EnergyPlus and Radiance require planar, well-segmented surfaces. Without careful preprocessing, models may produce unstable or misleading results. CurvAdapt implements a robust framework that unifies segmentation for NURBS and simplification for polylines, governed by the maximum chord error as a geometric fidelity criterion.

items.title: Segmentation
items.description: Adaptive conversion of NURBS into polylines using curvature-, tangent-, or error-driven strategies.

items.title: Simplification
items.description: Efficient reduction of polyline density with error bounds, based on Douglas–Peucker, Visvalingam–Whyatt, and angle-based methods.

items.title: Error Control
items.description: Guarantees geometric fidelity by reporting maximum chord error, ensuring reproducibility and comparability of results.

items.title: Simulation Integration
items.description: Produces leaner, simulation-ready geometry that reduces runtime in EnergyPlus and Radiance while maintaining accuracy.

content_blocks.title: The Problem of Non-Monotonic Convergence
content_blocks.subtitle: Why simulation accuracy does not always improve with more segments
content_blocks.content: Our research shows that relying on simulation outputs alone to judge simplification quality is flawed. Complex geometries exhibit non-monotonic convergence, where increasing detail can paradoxically worsen accuracy. To overcome this, CurvAdapt enforces a geometric guarantee via maximum chord error before simulation, ensuring stability and preventing 'false convergence.'

sections.title: Segmentation
sections.content: Uniform by length/parameter, curvature-based, tangent-angle based, and recursive Douglas–Peucker with kink preservation.

sections.title: Simplification
sections.content: Douglas–Peucker distance tolerance, Visvalingam–Whyatt area reduction, and angle-based filtering.

sections.title: Metrics
sections.content: Geometric fidelity measured by maximum chord error; simulation performance measured by deviation in radiation/energy results.

metrics.geometry_reduction: Vertex count reduced by up to 70%
